key_insight: TabPFN and TabICL are highly competitive out-of-the-box surrogate models for Bayesian optimization in materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: These tabular foundation models could simplify materials-search workflows by avoiding task-specific surrogate training and Gaussian-process kernel selection.
method: Use TabPFN and TabICL as Bayesian optimization surrogates.
Evaluate on two standard materials science benchmarks.
Compare against Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost.
evidence_signal: Across two materials science benchmarks, the abstract reports highly competitive performance against a broad baseline field, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Performance on two benchmarks does not establish reliability across other materials domains or experimental settings.
paper_title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
